entities.name: Ethyl ester reduction
observations: The encoded transformation converts an ethyl ester, CCOC(=O)–, into a primary hydroxymethyl group, –CH2OH, while retaining the N-substituted cyclic amine scaffold.
Standardized structures were reactant CCOC(=O)C1CCN(Cc2ccccc2)CC1 and product OCC1CCN(Cc2ccccc2)CC1.

entities.name: LiAlH4 ether reduction
observations: A directly matching record uses aluminum hydride/lithium hydride components in diethyl ether, consistent with lithium aluminum hydride reduction of the ester to the primary alcohol; aqueous/basic workup is indicated in a related record.

entities.name: Borane complexes
observations: BH3·THF and BH3·SMe2 are chemically plausible ester-to-primary-alcohol reducing systems, but no direct exact-substrate record was retrieved.

entities.name: DIBAL-H
observations: DIBAL-H commonly favors ester-to-aldehyde reduction under controlled low-temperature conditions; complete reduction to alcohol requires optimization, excess reagent, or more forcing conditions. No direct exact-substrate record was retrieved.
